title: PermissionRequested
description: The one `request` that travels server to client, and the reason the whole protocol is a socket instead of a stream: `canUseTool` has blocked the agent loop and it stays blocked until somebody answers or the deadline passes. Answered with the `permission.resolve` response.

requestId.description: Idempotency is by **this** field, never by `toolUseId`.

toolUseId.description: The invocation this request is about, tying it to the `tool.started` already on screen.

kind.description: The canonical kind of the call being asked about, exactly as its `tool.started` carries it — open: an unknown kind is drawn as the generic card.

label.description: The label of the call, as its `tool.started` carries it.

subject.description: What the call is about — the command, the paths, the URL.

changes.description: The files the call would change: a non-empty list turns on the preview, which the diff route serves while the request is pending (B-17).

origin.description: The engine and its own name for the tool — opaque, as on `tool.started`.

rawInput.description: The exact input the call would run with — what is shown is what executes. Opaque: drawn whole, never read field by field (plan 28, D-04).

title.description: An i18n key naming what is being asked, by kind — `permission.tool.<kind>` with the dots of the kind removed and the next letter upper-cased (`permission.tool.fileEdit`). A client without the key shows the translated `label`.

description.description: The detail a human needs to decide — the command line, the path being written.

riskHint.description: Derived in the backend, by the `kind` **plus** a heuristic over a `shell` command, and it fails closed: a command the heuristic does not recognise, and every kind outside the read and write lists, is `destructive`. A false positive is an annoyance; a false negative is the accident.

defaultToNo.description: The UI pre-selects refusal. Silence never authorises. `false` only on a question (`interaction`), where the focus goes to the first option.

expiresAt.description: When the request is denied automatically, ISO 8601 in UTC. Ours is the only timeout there is — the CLI imposes none.

suggestions.description: Scopes the UI may offer beyond a one-off yes. `project` and `always` come whenever the request has at least one reach in `reaches` (and `project` only with a workspace). Empty on a question: answering one leaves no rule.

labelKey.description: An i18n key. The server never sends prose.

pattern.description: What a rule granted with the `exact` reach would match, in the canonical grammar (`<kind>(<matcher>)`, plan 28, B-31). Kept for clients that do not read `reaches`; absent when there is no `exact` reach.

lifetimeMs.description: How long a rule granted by this suggestion would live, counted from the answer. Present on `project` and `always`; the number is the installation's, never the client's.

reaches.description: How far a rule left by this answer may reach, computed by the server from the invocation. The client picks one and answers with its `reach`, never with a pattern: the server computes the patterns again and refuses a reach it did not offer. Applies to `session`, `project` and `always`. Empty on a question.

reach.description: `exact` is this very call; `prefix` (`shell` only) covers every command that starts like each command of this line; `tool` (never `shell`) is every call of the kind.

patterns.description: The rules this reach would leave, one per pattern, in the canonical grammar — `shell(git status:*)`, `file.edit(src/a.ts)`, `web.fetch(domain:example.com)`, `mcp(srv:tool)`, or the bare kind. Shown in full before anybody confirms; the client treats them as text and never builds one.

interaction.description: Set when the request is a question rather than a permission. Absent on every other request.
